fact: The Ministry of Justice says CRIMS is under development, not yet in use: it is to record digitally everything from the crime report through investigation, charge, trial and sentence, with modules for report intake, investigation, juvenile offenders, offence type, biometric data, and prosecutors' and courts' decisions; no date is given for the forum, so the published date is used.

The Ministry of Justice says CRIMS is being developed by the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute for the ministry, the Federal Police Commission and the Addis Ababa Police Commission to work in jointly, steered by a coordinating committee whose forum the Minister of Justice attended; no finance is stated and the published date is used.

The Ministry of Justice reported a coordinating-committee forum, with the minister and senior leaders of the three bodies, at which CRIMS was said to be in development; the item gives no forum date, so its published date is used.

The Ministry of Justice says it is training federal investigating police and prosecutors in order to launch widely its criminal record management information system, which is to support the process from the crime report to sentencing; the first round lasts five days and about 100 investigators and prosecutors are to be trained in all; no event date is given, so the published date is used.

The Ministry of Justice runs the CRIMS training and names greater use of technology as one of its goals for the year, its state minister for institution building and reform addressing the trainees; no finance is stated and the published date is used.
